hints: Look at the large white oval in the centre, that is the bronchiole lumen. Find its longest distance across (maximum diameter) and measure it on the page in millimetres with a ruler.
Remember actual size = image size divided by magnification, then convert your answer from mm to micrometres by multiplying by 1000.
walkthrough:
**Spot what to measure**

First, find the bronchiole. It is the large oval tube in the middle, surrounded by thin-walled alveoli.

We want the maximum diameter of the lumen only. That means the white space inside, measured across its longest axis, not including the wall.

**Measure the image and apply magnification**

On a printed paper, this longest lumen diameter measures about $50 \text{ mm}$.

Use the magnification formula:
$$\text{actual size} = \frac{\text{image size}}{\text{magnification}}$$
$$\text{actual size} = \frac{50 \text{ mm}}{360} \approx 0.139 \text{ mm}$$

**Convert to micrometres and choose**

In cell biology we use micrometres for this size. Convert:
$$1 \text{ mm} = 1000 \, \mu\text{m}$$
$$0.139 \text{ mm} \times 1000 \approx 139 \, \mu\text{m}$$

This is closest to $140 \, \mu\text{m}$, so C is correct.

options.A: Too small by a factor of 10. This happens if you forget to multiply mm by 1000 correctly when converting to micrometres.
options.B: Too small. This is close to the minimum (short) diameter of the lumen, not the maximum diameter asked for.
options.C: Correct. An image size of about 50 mm divided by x360 gives about 0.14 mm, which is about 140 micrometres.
options.D: Too large. This happens if you measure to the outside of the bronchiole wall instead of the lumen only.
